question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards from the top of a tower with a velocity of $20\text{ m/s}$. The ball strikes the ground after $6\text{ s}$. The height of the tower is (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$): [IIT Adv. 2011]

A rocket is moving in a gravity-free space with a constant acceleration of $2\text{ m/s}^2$ along +x direction. The length of a chamber inside the rocket is $4\text{ m}$. A ball is thrown from the left wall of the chamber towards the right wall with a speed of $0.3\text{ m/s}$ relative to the rocket. At the same time, another ball is thrown from the right wall towards the left wall with a speed of $0.2\text{ m/s}$ relative to the rocket. The time in seconds when the two balls meet is: [IIT Adv. 2014]

A projectile is given an initial velocity of $(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j})\text{ m/s}$, where $\hat{i}$ is along the ground and $\hat{j}$ is along the vertical. If $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, the equation of its trajectory is: [IIT Adv. 2013]
A player kicks a football slanting upwards from the ground. Neglecting air resistance, the quantities that remain constant during the flight are: [IIT Adv. 2019]
options: Vertical component of velocity and total mechanical energy
Horizontal component of velocity and total mechanical energy
Horizontal component of velocity and vertical component of acceleration

question: Airplanes A and B are flying with constant velocities in the same vertical plane at angles $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ with respect to the horizontal respectively. The speed of A is $100\sqrt{3}\text{ m/s}$. An observer in A finds B flying along a line perpendicular to the line of motion of A. If at $t = 0$, A is at a distance of $500\text{ m}$ ahead of B, the time after which a collision could occur is: [IIT Adv. 2014]

From a tower of height $H$, a particle is thrown vertically upwards with a speed $u$. The time taken by the particle to hit the ground is $n$ times that taken by it to reach the highest point of its path. The relation between $H$, $u$, and $n$ is: [IIT Adv. 2014]

A particle moves in the $xy$-plane with a constant acceleration $a$ directed along the negative $y$-axis. The equation of motion of the particle has the form $y = px - qx^2$, where $p$ and $q$ are positive constants. The velocity of the particle at the origin of coordinates is: [IIT Adv. 2016]

A ball is projected from the ground at an angle of $45^\circ$ with the horizontal surface. It reaches a maximum height of $120\text{ m}$ and returns to the ground. The horizontal range of the projectile is: [IIT Adv. 2010]

The displacement $x$ of a particle moving in one dimension under the action of a constant force is related to time $t$ by the equation $t = \sqrt{x} + 3$, where $x$ is in meters and $t$ is in seconds. The displacement of the particle when its velocity is zero is: [IIT Adv. 2012]

A river is flowing from west to east at a speed of $5\text{ m/min}$. A man on the south bank of the river, capable of swimming at $10\text{ m/min}$ in still water, wants to swim across the river in the shortest time. He should swim in a direction: [IIT Adv. 2011]
A body is projected vertically upwards from the surface of the Earth with a velocity sufficient to carry it to infinity. The time taken by it to reach a height $h$ is proportional to: [IIT Adv. 2015]

A particle of mass $m$ moves on the $x$-axis as follows: it starts from rest at $t = 0$ from the point $x = 0$ and comes to rest at $t = 1$ at the point $x = 1$. No other information is available about its motion at intermediate times. If $\alpha$ denotes the instantaneous acceleration of the particle, then: [IIT Adv. 2018]
options: $\alpha$ cannot remain positive for all time in the interval $0 \le t \le 1$
|$\alpha$| cannot exceed 2 at any point in its path
$\alpha$ must change sign exactly once during the motion

question: A particle is dropped from a height $h$. Another particle is projected vertically up from the ground at the same instant such that they meet at the midpoint of the height $h$. The initial velocity of the second particle is: [IIT Adv. 2013]

A boy throws a ball upwards with velocity $v_0 = 20\text{ m/s}$. The wind imparts a constant horizontal acceleration of $4\text{ m/s}^2$ to the left. The horizontal distance from the starting point where the ball lands back on the ground is (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$): [IIT Adv. 2017]

The velocity-time graph of a stone thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of $30\text{ m/s}$ is a straight line. The total distance covered by the stone in the first $4\text{ s}$ of its motion is (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$): [IIT Adv. 2015]

A small block slides down a smooth inclined plane of inclination $\theta$ starting from rest. Let $S_n$ be the distance travelled by the block in the time interval $t = n-1$ to $t = n$. Then the ratio $S_n / S_{n+1}$ is: [IIT Adv. 2016]
A body starting from rest moves with uniform acceleration. The ratio of distance covered by the body as a function of time $t$ in successive equal time intervals is: [IIT Adv. 2012]

Two stones are thrown vertically upwards simultaneously from the same point on the ground with initial velocities $u_1 = 30\text{ m/s}$ and $u_2 = 50\text{ m/s}$. The maximum separation between them during their flight before the first stone hits the ground is (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$): [IIT Adv. 2019]
The position vector of a particle moving in the $xy$-plane is given by $\vec{r} = (A\sin\omega t)\hat{i} + (A\cos\omega t)\hat{j}$. The path traced by the particle is: [IIT Adv. 2014]
A bullet fired into a target loses half of its velocity after penetrating $3\text{ cm}$. How much further will it penetrate before coming to rest, assuming a constant resistive force? [IIT Adv. 2011]
